options.description: A record that restates or harmlessly extends your words is approved as judge-approved and you can reverse it in conversation; only a contradiction or new intent asks you. Most of the 415 waiting records would be approved.
options.label: Approve benign, ask on contradiction (Recommended)

options.description: The judge keeps asking whether your words entail the record; nearly every record keeps waiting for your answer, as today.
options.label: Keep entailment, raise nothing

options.description: As the first option, but only when the judge is confident (say 0.75); the uncertain rest still asks you.
options.label: Approve benign only above a confidence bar

payload.question: Your words are approximate and the records are formal, so a record almost never follows word for word from what you said. Today plumb's judge is asked whether your words entail the record, and it has answered no 803 times out of 803, so every record waits for you. Should the judge instead approve a record that adds nothing you would object to, and ask you only when it contradicts you or adds intent you did not give?
